claims.text: Conventional TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an α+β dual-phase microstructure.
Conventional TC4 has a typical hardness of approximately 240 HV.
Conventional TC4 has inadequate wear resistance.
Pulsed laser surface nitriding in a nitrogen-rich atmosphere will produce a TiN-reinforced surface layer on TC4.
The resulting TiN-rich layer will be uniform and adherent.
The resulting TiN-rich layer will be nanocrystalline.
Rapid solidification following laser treatment will refine the grain structure of the modified layer.
Optimizing laser pulse duration and energy density will maximize TiN formation and adhesion while limiting the heat-affected zone.
A hard, refined, well-adhered TiN-rich surface layer will increase the surface hardness of TC4.
A hard, refined, well-adhered TiN-rich surface layer will reduce wear of TC4.
Laser surface nitriding will increase TC4 surface hardness by at least 50% relative to untreated TC4.
The hardness is predicted to increase from approximately 240 HV to greater than 350 HV.
Laser-nitrided TC4 will have shallower wear tracks than untreated TC4.
Laser-nitrided TC4 will exhibit less material loss than untreated TC4 in reciprocating or sliding wear tests.
The treatment will preserve the bulk corrosion resistance of TC4.
The treatment will preserve the bulk toughness of TC4.
The treated surface will remain effective in wear testing or operation from ambient temperature to approximately 300°C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 50% hardness increase, but the illustrative change from approximately 240 HV to merely greater than 350 HV does not necessarily meet that threshold; a 50% increase from 240 HV requires at least 360 HV.
